newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemeni tribesmen release German hostages.
newsitem.headline: Yemeni tribesmen release German hostages.

text.p: Tribesmen in Yemen early on Tuesday released seven German tourists they had been holding for a week, a Yemeni security official said.
He told Reuters a plane left for the eastern province of Hadramaut, 770 km (480 miles) east of Sanaa, to fly them back to the Yemeni capital.
No other details were immediately available.
The seven men aged between 30 and 45 were kidnapped last week while riding motorcycles through the Wadi al-Dabaat area between Mahra and Hadramaut provinces.
A security official had said earlier on Tuesday that the kidnappers agreed to release the Germans after security forces and troops tightened a siege on them.

He would not say whether the abductors, who sought to pressure the government to bring to justice an alleged Yemeni swindler who sold them smuggled cars brought in from Gulf Arab states, had dropped their demands.
Security sources had said the abductors had telephoned local authorities to demand 12 million marks ($7 million) ransom for releasing the tourists, but police in Hadramaut denied that.
Yemeni Interior Minister Hussein Mohammad Arab told the German ambassador on Monday the seven were in good health.
Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners in recent years to use as bargaining chips.
An American diplomat and a Saudi ambassador have been among the kidnap victims. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions and all the hostages have been released unharmed.
Some were rescued by security forces, others were set free.
